page: Microsoft Azure D2as_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, operating under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system allocates 2 vCPUs derived from a single dedicated physical core of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz with simultaneous multithreading. Memory is provisioned at 8.0 GB, resulting in 4.0 GB per vCPU, accompanied by a 32 MB L3 cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1 data cache. The instance includes 17 GB of local SSD storage, contains zero GPUs, and provides no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate competitive single-threaded execution alongside hardware-constrained multi-threaded output. The server achieves a stress-ng single-core rating in the top 25 percent and mid-tier performance across Geekbench single-core, single-threaded gzip compression at 26.07 GB/sec, and bzip3 decompression at 11.24 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded results scale strictly within the two-vCPU ceiling, placing Geekbench multi-core, PassMark CPU, and Redis SET throughput within the lowest 10 percent of evaluated systems. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks register 33.11 GB/sec for reads and 22.43 GB/sec for writes.

The primary tradeoff of this instance centers on restricted parallel capacity and modest local storage. While the AMD EPYC core provides responsive execution for serialized operations, the small virtual core count and memory pool limit high-concurrency demands. Consequently, the virtual machine delivers effective resource density for lightweight microservices, small API endpoints, background automation jobs, and software development sandboxes rather than dense enterprise databases or multi-threaded build farms.
description: Microsoft Azure D2as_v4 is a general-purpose instance configured with 2 vCPUs and 8 GB of memory, delivering a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the virtual machine runs on an AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz, allocating one physical core with two execution threads, supported by a 32 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 17 GB of local SSD storage and operates without an attached discrete GPU accelerator. Performance benchmarks reflect strong single-core compute capabilities, highlighted by a stress-ng single-core score in the top 25 percent and competitive decompression throughput. However, its small core count limits aggregate multi-threaded operations, showing bottom-tier scores in multi-core compiling, ray tracing, and static web serving throughput. Cost efficiency is driven by its compact resource footprint, making it suitable for low-concurrency web serving, basic background services, microservices, and lightweight development environments.
